/-!
# Cullen primes

A Cullen number is a natural number of the form $C_n = n \cdot 2^n + 1$.

*Reference:*
- [Wikipedia, Cullen number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cullen_number)
-/

namespace CullenPrime

/-- There are infinitely many natural numbers $n$ for which the Cullen number
$C_n = n \cdot 2^n + 1$ is prime; that is, there are infinitely many Cullen primes. -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem cullen_prime : Set.Infinite {n : ℕ | (n * 2 ^ n + 1).Prime} := by
  sorry

end CullenPrime
modeling_decisions: Interpreted the terse list-page question using the Cullen-number article's definition C_n = n * 2^n + 1 and its explicit statement that infinitude is conjectured, so the theorem directly states the positive conjecture.

Expressed infinitude as Set.Infinite {n : ℕ | (n * 2 ^ n + 1).Prime}, as required by the decomposition. This counts prime-producing indices; this is equivalent to counting Cullen prime values because the Cullen-number sequence is strictly increasing.
Included n = 0 in the natural-number index domain. It contributes C_0 = 1, which is not prime, so it does not affect infinitude.
Did not include the distinct open question asking whether C_p is prime for some prime index p.

/-!

A Cullen number is a number of the form $C_n = n \cdot 2^n + 1$ with $n$ a natural number.
A Cullen prime is a Cullen number that is prime. Only sixteen Cullen primes are known, and
it is conjectured that there are infinitely many.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Cullen number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cullen_number)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [OEIS A005849](https://oeis.org/A005849)
-/

namespace CullenPrime

/-- The smallest Cullen prime is $C_1 = 1 \cdot 2^1 + 1 = 3$. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem one_mem : 1 ∈ {n : ℕ | (n * 2 ^ n + 1).Prime} := by
  norm_num

/-- There are infinitely many Cullen primes, i.e. there are infinitely many $n$ for which the
Cullen number $C_n = n \cdot 2^n + 1$ is prime. -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem cullen_prime : {n : ℕ | (n * 2 ^ n + 1).Prime}.Infinite := by
  sorry

end CullenPrime
